revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Louvre Pyramid
revealWordProblem.text: The Louvre Pyramid in Paris is a square pyramid made of glass panels. How could you use a net and the surface area formula to find the total area of glass in its four triangular faces?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Unfold the pyramid into a net: the square base separates from the four triangular faces so each one lies flat and can be measured on its own. Since the question only asks about the glass in the four triangular faces, find the area of one triangular face using ½ × base edge × slant height, then multiply by 4 — the base square is not part of this total. For example, if the base edge is 6 ft and the slant height is 8 ft, one triangular face is ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 ft², so the four faces together need 4 × 24 = 96 ft² of glass.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do we find the surface area of a pyramid?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Surface area of a pyramid = base area + the area of all the triangular lateral faces — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My square pyramid has a 6 × 6 base and a slant height of 8.
Now one triangular face: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24. A square pyramid has 4 of them, so 4 × 24 = 96.
I add the base and the side faces: 36 + 96 = 132.
So the total surface area is 132 in². I used the slant height (8) for the triangles, not the pyramid's height.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Calculate the surface area of each pyramid display. SA = Base Area + Lateral Area. For each triangular face, use A = ½ × base × slant height. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

onLevel.stem: A square pyramid has a base area of 49 cm² and a total lateral area of 84 cm². What is the surface area?
onLevel.explanation: SA = Base Area + Lateral Area = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².
choiceFeedback: That's just the lateral area — add the base area too for total surface area.
That's just the base area — add the lateral (triangular) area too for the total.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Both pieces are already given: base area 49 cm² and lateral (triangle) area 84 cm².
Total surface area = base area + lateral area — one addition, keeping square units.
Set up the sum 49 + 84 and add carefully, keeping cm² in your answer.
onLevel.stemEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene un área de base de 49 cm² y un área lateral total de 84 cm². ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
onLevel.explanationEs: Área de superficie = área de la base + área lateral = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².
hintsEs: Ya te dan las dos piezas: área de la base 49 cm² y área lateral (de los triángulos) 84 cm².
Área superficial total = área de la base + área lateral: una sola suma, conservando las unidades cuadradas.
Plantea la suma 49 + 84 y súmala con cuidado, conservando cm² en tu respuesta.

onLevel.title: Did You Halve the Triangle?

workedExample.label: Box
workedExample.work: Square pyramid: base edge = 8 in, slant height = 10 in
workedExample.workEs: Pirámide cuadrada: arista de la base = 8 pulg, altura inclinada = 10 pulg

onLevel.correctWork: A triangle's area is ½ × base × height, so each face is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², not 80 in². The student left out the ½. Four faces: 4 × 40 = 160 in². Correct SA = 64 + 160 = 224 in².
hints: Look at the triangular-face step — what is the area formula for a triangle?
Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. Each face is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², so SA = 64 + 4 × 40 = 224 in².
onLevel.explanation: The face step multiplied 8 × 10 = 80 in², which is the area of a whole rectangle, not a triangle. A triangle is half of that rectangle, so each face is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², four faces give 160 in², and the correct total is SA = 64 + 160 = 224 in².
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la cara multiplicó 8 × 10 = 80 in², que es el área de un rectángulo completo, no de un triángulo. Un triángulo es la mitad de ese rectángulo, así que cada cara es ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², cuatro caras dan 160 in² y el total correcto es SA = 64 + 160 = 224 in².
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El área de un triángulo es ½ × base × altura, así que cada cara es ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², no 80 in². El estudiante omitió el ½. Cuatro caras: 4 × 40 = 160 in². SA correcta = 64 + 160 = 224 in².
hintsEs: Mira el paso de la cara triangular — ¿cuál es la fórmula del área de un triángulo?
Área de un triángulo = ½ × base × altura. Cada cara es ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 pulg², así que el área total es 64 + 4 × 40 = 224 pulg².

onLevel.title: Find the Surface Area Error

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: Square pyramid: base edge = 10 in, slant height = 8 in
workedExample.workEs: Pirámide cuadrada: arista de la base = 10 pulg, altura inclinada = 8 pulg

workedExample.label: Lateral Area
workedExample.work: ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in² (one face). Total lateral = 40 × 3 = 120 in²
workedExample.workEs: ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in² (una cara). Lateral total = 40 × 3 = 120 in²

onLevel.correctWork: A square pyramid has 4 lateral faces, not 3. Total lateral = 40 × 4 = 160 in². Correct: SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
hints: Check Step 3: how many lateral faces does a square pyramid have?
A square base has 4 sides, so there are 4 triangular faces. The student only multiplied by 3.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error de área total
onLevel.explanation: The area of one face, ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in², is right, but it was multiplied by 3 instead of 4. A square base has four sides, so four triangles meet at the top: 40 × 4 = 160 in², and SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
onLevel.explanationEs: El área de una cara, ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in², está bien, pero se multiplicó por 3 en vez de por 4. Una base cuadrada tiene cuatro lados, así que cuatro triángulos se juntan en la punta: 40 × 4 = 160 in², y SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene 4 caras laterales, no 3. Lateral total = 40 × 4 = 160 in². Correcto: SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
hintsEs: Revisa el Paso 3: ¿cuántas caras laterales tiene una pirámide de base cuadrada?
Una base cuadrada tiene 4 lados, así que hay 4 caras triangulares. El estudiante solo multiplicó por 3.

onLevel.prompt: Two pyramids have the same base area (64 in²) but different slant heights. Pyramid A has slant height 6 in and Pyramid B has slant height 10 in. How much more surface area does Pyramid B have? Why does slant height affect surface area but NOT base area?
onLevel.sentenceFrame: Pyramid A: SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 6) = 64 + ___ = ___ in². Pyramid B: SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 10) = 64 + ___ = ___ in². Pyramid B has ___ more in² because ___. Slant height only affects ___ because ___.
onLevel.hint: Find each pyramid's surface area, then compare the totals.
hints: Both pyramids share a 64 in² base (edge 8 in). Only the slant heights differ: 6 in versus 10 in.
Find each SA = 64 + 4 × (½ × 8 × slant height), then subtract the totals. The base never uses the slant height.
Pyramid A first: one triangle is ½ × 8 × 6. Multiply by 4, add 64, then repeat using slant height 10.
onLevel.explanation: With a 64 in² base the edge is 8 in, so Pyramid A has SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 6) = 64 + 96 = 160 in² and Pyramid B has SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 10) = 64 + 160 = 224 in², a difference of 64 in². Slant height only appears in the triangle formula, so it stretches the lateral faces while the base area stays 8 × 8 no matter how tall the pyramid gets.
onLevel.explanationEs: Con una base de 64 in² la arista mide 8 in, así que la Pirámide A tiene SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 6) = 64 + 96 = 160 in² y la Pirámide B tiene SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 10) = 64 + 160 = 224 in², una diferencia de 64 in². La altura inclinada solo aparece en la fórmula del triángulo, así que estira las caras laterales mientras el área de la base sigue siendo 8 × 8 sin importar cuánto suba la pirámide.
onLevel.promptEs: Dos pirámides tienen la misma área de base (64 in²) pero alturas inclinadas diferentes. La pirámide A tiene una altura inclinada de 6 in y la pirámide B de 10 in. ¿Cuánta área superficial más tiene la pirámide B? ¿Por qué la altura inclinada afecta el área superficial pero NO el área de la base?
hintsEs: Ambas pirámides comparten una base de 64 pulg² (arista de 8 pulg). Solo cambian las apotemas: 6 pulg frente a 10 pulg.
Halla cada AS = 64 + 4 × (½ × 8 × apotema) y luego resta los totales. La base nunca usa la apotema.
Pirámide A primero: un triángulo es ½ × 8 × 6. Multiplica por 4, suma 64 y luego repite con la apotema de 10.

extending.stem: Your first gift box is a square pyramid with a base edge of 7 in and a slant height of 9 in. How much wrapping paper (total surface area) covers it?
extending.explanation: Base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². One triangular face: ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 31.5 = 126 in². SA = 49 + 126 = 175 in². Surface area uses square units (in²).
choiceFeedback: You found the four triangular faces but forgot to add the square base.
Recalculate the base area (side × side) and each triangular face separately before adding.
Check the units — wrapping paper covers a surface, so it needs square units, not cubic.
extending.stemEs: Tu primera caja de regalo es una pirámide cuadrada con una arista de base de 7 in y una altura inclinada de 9 in. ¿Cuánto papel de regalo (área de superficie total) la cubre?
extending.explanationEs: Base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². Una cara triangular: ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². Cuatro caras: 4 × 31.5 = 126 in². Área de superficie = 49 + 126 = 175 in². El área de superficie usa unidades cuadradas (in²).
hints: Wrapping paper has to cover every face you could touch: the square base plus all four triangles.
Find the base area first, then the area of one triangular face, then multiply that face by how many lateral faces there are before you add.
Start with the base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². One triangular face is ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². How many of those triangles are there, and what do you still add?
hintsEs: El papel de regalo tiene que cubrir todas las caras que puedes tocar: la base cuadrada más las cuatro caras triangulares.
Halla primero el área de la base, luego el área de una cara triangular, y después multiplica esa cara por el número de caras laterales antes de sumar.
Empieza con la base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². Una cara triangular es ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². ¿Cuántos triángulos como ese hay, y qué te falta sumar?

extending.stem: Before adding the base, you need the area of just one triangular face of a gift box with base edge 8 in and slant height 5 in. What is it?
extending.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 in². You use the slant height (5) as the triangle's height, not the pyramid's vertical height.
choiceFeedback: Don't forget to take half — a triangle's area is half of base times height.
Adding the base and height together won't give area — multiply them, then take half.
Check the units — a flat triangular face is measured in square units, not cubic.
extending.stemEs: Antes de sumar la base, necesitas el área de una sola cara triangular de una caja de regalo con arista de base de 8 in y altura inclinada de 5 in. ¿Cuál es?
extending.explanationEs: Área de un triángulo = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 in². Usas la altura inclinada (5) como altura del triángulo, no la altura vertical de la pirámide.
hints: A lateral face of a pyramid is a triangle, and a triangle's area is half of base × height.
The slant height acts as the triangle's height here, and the square base is not part of this step at all.
Multiply base × slant height first: 8 × 5 = 40. A triangle covers only half of that rectangle — finish the last step.
hintsEs: Una cara lateral de una pirámide es un triángulo, y el área de un triángulo es la mitad de base × altura.
Aquí la altura inclinada funciona como la altura del triángulo, y la base cuadrada no entra en este paso.
Multiplica primero base × altura inclinada: 8 × 5 = 40. Un triángulo cubre solo la mitad de ese rectángulo: termina el último paso.

extending.stem: A gift box is a square pyramid with a base edge of 9 in. What is the area of its square base (the part that sits on the table)?
extending.explanation: The base is a square, so base area = side × side = 9 × 9 = 81 in². You would still add the four triangular faces to get the full surface area.
choiceFeedback: That looks like a perimeter calculation — area of a square is side × side, not side × 4.
Doubling the side length isn't the same as squaring it — multiply the side by itself.
That includes extra faces — the base area alone only needs side × side, not four times that.
extending.stemEs: Una caja de regalo es una pirámide cuadrada con una arista de base de 9 in. ¿Cuál es el área de su base cuadrada (la parte que se apoya en la mesa)?
extending.explanationEs: La base es un cuadrado, así que el área de la base = lado × lado = 9 × 9 = 81 in². Todavía tendrías que sumar las cuatro caras triangulares para obtener el área de superficie total.
hints: The base of a square pyramid is a square, and every side of a square has the same length.
The area of a square is side × side, so no slant height is needed for this part.
Both sides of the base measure 9 in, so set up 9 × 9 and compute it.
hintsEs: La base de una pirámide cuadrada es un cuadrado, y todos los lados de un cuadrado miden lo mismo.
El área de un cuadrado es lado × lado, así que no se necesita la altura inclinada en esta parte.
Los dos lados de la base miden 9 in, así que plantea 9 × 9 y calcúlalo.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — Slant Height vs. Base Edge

workedExample.label: Box
workedExample.work: Square pyramid gift box: base edge = 12 in, slant height = 9 in
workedExample.workEs: Caja de regalo de pirámide cuadrada: arista de la base = 12 pulg, altura inclinada = 9 pulg

extending.correctWork: Each triangular face uses the base edge (12) as its base and the slant height (9) as its height: ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 in². The student used the slant height (9) in place of the base edge by mistake. Four faces: 4 × 54 = 216 in². Correct SA = 144 + 216 = 360 in².
hints: Check the triangular-face step: which number is the triangle's base, and which is its height?
The triangle's base is the base edge (12 in) and its height is the slant height (9 in). The student used 9 twice instead of 12 and 9.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Altura inclinada contra arista de la base
extending.explanation: The face step used 9 twice, but a lateral triangle takes its base from the base edge (12 in) and its height from the slant height (9 in), so each face is ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 in², not 40.5 in². Four faces give 216 in², and the correct total is SA = 144 + 216 = 360 in².
extending.explanationEs: El paso de la cara usó 9 dos veces, pero un triángulo lateral toma su base de la arista de la base (12 in) y su altura de la altura inclinada (9 in), así que cada cara es ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 in², no 40.5 in². Cuatro caras dan 216 in², y el total correcto es SA = 144 + 216 = 360 in².
extending.correctWorkEs: Cada cara triangular usa la arista de la base (12) como base y la altura inclinada (9) como altura: ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 in². El estudiante usó la altura inclinada (9) en lugar de la arista de la base por error. Cuatro caras: 4 × 54 = 216 in². SA correcta = 144 + 216 = 360 in².
hintsEs: Revisa el paso de la cara triangular: ¿cuál número es la base del triángulo y cuál es su altura?
La base del triángulo es la arista de la base (12 pulg) y su altura es la altura inclinada (9 pulg). El estudiante usó 9 dos veces en vez de 12 y 9.

extending.stem: A square pyramid has a base edge of 5 in and a slant height of 7 in. What is the surface area?
extending.explanation: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². SA = 25 + 70 = 95 in².
choiceFeedback: You calculated the four triangular faces but forgot to add the square base area.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
Recheck each triangular face area — make sure you take half of base times slant height for each.
hints: A square pyramid has TWO kinds of faces: one square base (5 × 5) and four identical triangles with slant height 7.
SA = base area + 4 triangle areas, where each triangle is ½ × base edge × slant height.
Base first: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Then one triangle: ½ × 5 × 7. Multiply that by 4 and add the base area.
extending.stemEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene una arista de base de 5 in y una altura inclinada de 7 in. ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
extending.explanationEs: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Cada cara lateral: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Cuatro caras: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². Área de superficie = 25 + 70 = 95 in².
hintsEs: Una pirámide cuadrangular tiene DOS tipos de caras: una base cuadrada (5 × 5) y cuatro triángulos idénticos con apotema de 7.
AS = área de la base + 4 áreas de triángulo, donde cada triángulo es ½ × arista de la base × apotema.
La base primero: 5 × 5 = 25 pulg². Luego un triángulo: ½ × 5 × 7. Multiplica eso por 4 y súmale el área de la base.

extending.stem: How many lateral (triangular) faces does a square pyramid have?
extending.explanation: A square pyramid has a square base and 4 triangular lateral faces — one for each side of the square.
choiceFeedback: A square base has four sides — count a triangular face for each side of the square.
The square base isn't a lateral (triangular) face — only count the slanted triangle sides.
That's too many — count only the slanted triangular sides around the square base.
hints: Lateral faces are the slanted triangles on the sides — the square base itself doesn't count.
Each side of the square base holds up exactly one triangle. Count the sides of a square.
Trace the base: it's a square. Count one triangle leaning against each side of that square.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuántas caras laterales (triangulares) tiene una pirámide cuadrada?
extending.explanationEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene una base cuadrada y 4 caras laterales triangulares, una por cada lado del cuadrado.
hintsEs: Las caras laterales son los triángulos inclinados de los lados; la base cuadrada no cuenta.
Cada lado de la base cuadrada sostiene exactamente un triángulo. Cuenta los lados de un cuadrado.
Traza la base: es un cuadrado. Cuenta un triángulo apoyado en cada lado de ese cuadrado.

extending.stem: What is the area of one triangular face with base 8 in and slant height 6 in?
extending.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in².
choiceFeedback: Don't forget to take half — a triangle's area is half of base times height, not the full product.
Adding the base and height won't give area — multiply them first, then take half.
Check the units — a flat triangular face needs square units, not cubic.
hints: You have one triangle: base 8 in, slant height 6 in. Triangle area is not just base × height.
Use area = ½ × base × height — multiply the two numbers first, then take half.
Multiply 8 × 6 = 48 first. Then take half of that result.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de una cara triangular con base de 8 in y altura inclinada de 6 in?
extending.explanationEs: Área de un triángulo = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in².
hintsEs: Tienes un triángulo: base 8 pulg, apotema 6 pulg. El área del triángulo no es solo base × altura.
Usa área = ½ × base × altura: multiplica primero los dos números y luego saca la mitad.
Multiplica 8 × 6 = 48 primero. Luego saca la mitad de ese resultado.

extending.correctWork: The student found the lateral area (60 in²) but forgot to add the base. Base area = 5 × 5 = 25 in². Correct SA = base + lateral = 25 + 60 = 85 in².
hints: Did the student include the bottom of the pyramid?
Surface area = base area + lateral area. Add the base: 25 + 60 = 85 in².
extending.explanation: The triangle work is right — each face is ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 in² and four faces give 60 in² — but the answer stops at the lateral area. Surface area covers the whole solid, so the 5 × 5 = 25 in² square base still has to be added, making SA = 25 + 60 = 85 in².
extending.explanationEs: El trabajo con los triángulos está bien —cada cara es ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 in² y cuatro caras dan 60 in²— pero la respuesta se detiene en el área lateral. El área total cubre todo el cuerpo, así que todavía hay que sumar la base cuadrada de 5 × 5 = 25 in², de modo que SA = 25 + 60 = 85 in².
extending.correctWorkEs: El estudiante encontró el área lateral (60 in²) pero olvidó sumar la base. Área de la base = 5 × 5 = 25 in². SA correcta = base + lateral = 25 + 60 = 85 in².
hintsEs: ¿El estudiante incluyó la base de la pirámide?
Área total = área de la base + área lateral. Suma la base: 25 + 60 = 85 pulg².

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Surface Area of Pyramids is finding the four triangular lateral faces correctly (½ × base edge × slant height, times 4) and then stopping — forgetting to add the base area at the end. This leaves the total surface area too small by exactly the base's area. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I add the base area to the four lateral faces, or did I stop after the sides?'

diagram.title: Glass Faces of the Display Case
diagram.caption: Each bar is one face's area in ft²; the open base adds 0 and the four triangular faces (½×3×4 = 6 ft² each) add up to 24 ft² of glass.

connect.scenario: A museum is building a square pyramid display case. The base edge is 3 feet and the slant height is 4 feet. The glass costs $12 per square foot.
connect.promptQuestion: How much will the glass for all 4 triangular sides cost? (The base is open — no glass needed.)
connect.prompt: Each triangular face has area = ½ × ___ × ___ = ___ ft². Four faces: 4 × ___ = ___ ft². Cost: ___ × $12 = $___.

check.stem: What is the area of one triangular face?
check.explanation: A = ½ × base × slant height = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 ft².

check.stem: What is the total glass area for all four faces?
check.explanation: 4 × 6 = 24 ft². The base is open, so it adds 0.

connect.modelAnswer: Each triangular face is ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 ft², and there are 4 of them: 4 × 6 = 24 ft² of glass (the base is open, so it needs none). At $12 per square foot the glass costs 24 × $12 = $288.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — A square pyramid has a base edge of 6 in and a slant height of 5 in. What is the total surface area?
exitTicket.explanation: Base: 6 × 6 = 36 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 in². Four faces: 4 × 15 = 60 in². SA = 36 + 60 = 96 in². Surface area uses square units (in²).
choiceFeedback: Add the base area too — total surface is base plus 4 triangles.
Surface area is square units (in²), not cubic.
That's only the base — include the four triangular faces.
hints: Two parts make the total: a 6 × 6 square base plus 4 triangles with base 6 and slant height 5.
SA = base area + 4 × (½ × base edge × slant height). Don't stop after the triangles — include the base.
Base: 6 × 6 = 36 in². One triangle: ½ × 6 × 5. Find it, multiply by 4, then add to the base area.
